title: Third-party rights, delegation, and assignment: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Lawrence v. Fox: The three people perform different legal roles. Keeping those roles explicit explains how consideration can support a promise while someone other than its promisee enforces it.

Seaver v. Ransom: Seaver extends beneficiary protection beyond the debt-discharge setting in Lawrence v. Fox. It distinguishes a gift intended for the beneficiary from an unsupported gift promise between the actual contracting parties.

Sisney v. State: The comparison with Sisney v. Reisch is essential. The same inmate and similar food problem produced a different result under a different agreement.

Sisney v. Reisch: Together the two Sisney decisions isolate the importance of identifying the precise contract, its beneficiaries, the defendant’s duty, and the procedural posture.
